note: Random encounter dialogue (D-105): the trees the enc_* NPCs use and their barks. A node's "encounter" key names an action in that encounter's definition (data/encounters/encounters.json), run by EncounterDirector. Placeholder text: edit freely.

encdriver_idle: It's the alternator. I think. I don't know what an alternator is.
Five years and it picks today.
encsales_idle: I walked here. From Grand Island. Ask me about it.
No refunds, no returns, no questions, no promises.
enctoll_idle: Road's maintained. By me. Hence the toll.
Ten caps or a long walk.
I take caps, bullets, or offence.
enccamp_idle: I've seen things. Most of them were cows.
There's a man in a suit walks the county line. Don't wave at him.
encpool_idle: Winner stays. I've stayed four years.
I'll spot you the break. I won't spot you anything else.
encbeg_idle: I'm not proud. I was. It didn't keep.
encwant_idle: Not a care in the world.
enctour_idle: The kids are being very patient.
encdrunk_idle: This is my barrel. I found it. It's my barrel.
encgamb_idle: Cards don't know it's the end of the world.
I'm due. I've been due since March.
encgamb_greet: Take a seat, take a chance.
enccoll_idle: Cones, ducks, little cars. I pay.
It's not hoarding if it's catalogued.
Somebody has to keep the stuff.
enccon_idle: This map has a vault on it. A VAULT.
enccon_greet: Friend! You look like an explorer.
encwand_idle: I've been through here before. You weren't here.
encgreg_idle: I had a thing. It was shaped like a thing.
My cart's got a wheel. It's got four. One's a wheel.
encinsp_idle: This whole county is out of compliance.
encbarg_idle: EVERYTHING MUST GO. SLOWLY. AT THESE PRICES.
You won't find this deal anywhere. Anywhere.
encsher_idle: Population one. Crime rate zero. You do the math.
I keep the peace. The peace keeps itself, mostly.
encchess_idle: That's a book line. Everything's a book line.
enccone_idle: Every cone in this town was placed by somebody. Somebody is me.
enccone_greet: Halt. You are in the Kingdom.

start.speaker: Marla
start.text: Oh thank God, a person. It died coming up the hill and it won't turn over. I'm two hundred miles from where I'm supposed to be and I don't even know what that place is called any more.

choices.text: I can fix that. (2 scrap metal, duct tape)
It's out of gas. I've got a can.
Nice car. I'll be taking it.

fixed.speaker: Marla
fixed.text: ...That's it? That's IT? Take this. Take all of it. I've been sat here since yesterday arguing with a hose.

gassed.speaker: Marla
gassed.text: Gas. It was gas. I'm a doctor, you know. Was. Take the glovebox, please, I insist.

robbed.speaker: Marla
robbed.text: No. No, no - BRANDON! BRANDON, IT'S HAPPENING AGAIN!

start.speaker: Dub
start.text: Dub's Rolling Emporium. I carry what fits in the cart and the cart fits what sells. What are we looking at today?

trade_food.speaker: Dub
trade_food.text: Beans. The good beans. The label's gone but I believe in them.

trade_ammo.speaker: Dub
trade_ammo.text: Nine mil. Hand loaded by a man I trust about half of.

trade_weird.speaker: Dub
trade_weird.text: No description. That's the deal. That's why it's twelve.

buy_scrap.speaker: Dub
buy_scrap.text: Scrap I can always move. Here's your caps.

broke.speaker: Dub
broke.text: That's a no from the cart, friend.

bye.speaker: Dub
bye.text: Browse away. The cart doesn't judge. I do, a little.

start.speaker: Cheryl
start.text: Road's closed. Well - road's priced. Ten caps and the barrel moves. That's the whole business model.

choices.text: There's twelve of us. The rest are behind me.

paid.speaker: Cheryl
paid.text: Pleasure doing business. Mind the ditch, there's a guy living in it.

start.speaker: Odell
start.text: Sit if you're sitting. I've got coffee that's mostly chicory and three stories that are mostly true.

choices.text: Who's the man in the suit?
Settle something for me: dent corn or flint corn?

rumor.speaker: Odell
rumor.text: Folks keep finding a lawn chair out on the flats with a fella still in it, cooler beside him, radio on. Chair moves. Fella don't. Make of that what you like.

rumor2.speaker: Odell
rumor2.text: There's a woman south of the tracks collects junk - cones, ducks, little cars. Pays real goods for it. I'd call her crazy but she's eating better than me.

suit.speaker: Odell
suit.text: Stands too far off to shout at. Doesn't move when you wave. Gets closer when you're not counting. ...You've seen him, haven't you. It's all right. We all have.

bye.speaker: Odell
bye.text: Mind the embers. Everybody says that. Nobody minds the embers.

q_corn_a.speaker: Dale
q_corn_a.text: Flint. I grew it, I dried it, I ate it for two years. Anybody says dent either never farmed or is lying for sport.

start.speaker: Fast Eddie
start.text: Haugen. They called me Fast Eddie before it was funny. Ten caps a game, winner takes twenty-five. Table's right there.

choices.text: Can I just shoot a few?

free.speaker: Fast Eddie
free.text: Be my guest. Nobody's stopping you. Nobody ever stops you. That's the sad part.

bye.speaker: Fast Eddie
bye.text: Table'll be here. So will I.

q_pool.speaker: Fast Eddie
q_pool.text: Nobody's beaten me. Not once, not before, not after. You can be the first. You won't be.

q_pool_in.speaker: Fast Eddie
q_pool_in.text: You watch him rack. The eight sits a half inch left of where he put it. There is a magnet under the felt and his hand keeps finding the rail.

choices.text: There's a magnet under your table, Eddie.

q_pool_caught.speaker: Fast Eddie
q_pool_caught.text: A long silence. Then, with enormous dignity: "It's a weighted table. There's a difference." He pays you to go away.

start.speaker: Pete
start.text: Spare anything? Food, water, a minute. I'm not fussy about which.

choices.text: Here, take a can of beans.

food.speaker: Pete
food.text: ...I'm going to be honest with you, I've got caps. I just wanted somebody to hand me something. Take them. Please.

water.speaker: Pete
water.text: You're the first one in a month. Here. It still turns on. I don't want to hear it ring again.

refuse.speaker: Pete
refuse.text: That's all right. That's all right.

q_donut.speaker: Pete
q_donut.text: Is that the donut? From the case? Pete's hands come up like he is being arrested. "People have died over that donut. I'm people."

q_donut_paid.speaker: Pete
q_donut_paid.text: He eats it in two bites, chews for a long time, and says, with total honesty, "It was better as an idea."

start.speaker: Dale
start.text: Afternoon. Beer? It's terrible. Sit anywhere.

choices.text: You're on a poster in four towns.

poster.speaker: Dale
poster.text: ...Is it the one where I'm squinting? I hate that one. So. What's it going to be.

walk.speaker: Dale
walk.text: Decent of you. There's a cooler under the chair, help yourself.

start.speaker: Sandy
start.text: Thank goodness. Do you know when they're reopening I-80? We've been in this rest stop a while and the radio's just doing that noise.

truth.speaker: Sandy
truth.text: ...Five. ...Right. Okay. Okay. Would you take this? It's Dylan's. He won't need it on the drive back. There isn't a drive back, is there.

play.speaker: Sandy
play.text: Oh, that's a relief. Here, for your trouble - we've got loads, we packed for a week.

bye.speaker: Sandy
bye.text: No, no, that's all right. Somebody will come.

start.speaker: Buzz
start.text: You! You look like a man who can hold his warm beer. Or a woman. Or whatever's going on there, I'm not judging, I'm SWAYING.

bye.speaker: Buzz
bye.text: You're my best friend. I'll forget this. Don't take it personal.

q_chair.speaker: Buzz
q_chair.text: Tournament rules: two chairs, one cooler, nobody stands up. I am the reigning champion of this and nine other things. Ten caps to enter.

choices.text: [10 caps] Set up the second chair.

q_chair_in.speaker: Buzz
q_chair_in.text: He produces a trophy from under the chair. It is a bowling trophy with the name filed off. "Undisputed. Don't let it change you."

start.speaker: Lucky
start.text: Five caps a hand, twenty-five if you're feeling brave. I deal, you cut, nobody shoots anybody. That's the whole rulebook.

bye.speaker: Lucky
bye.text: Everybody gambles. Most people just don't get a table.

start.speaker: Winifred
start.text: Winifred. I buy oddities - cones, ducks, gnomes, pins, plates, tapes, the little cars. The world ended and everyone started collecting bullets. Somebody has to keep the STUFF.

choices.text: I walked through a door in a field.

paid_good.speaker: Winifred
paid_good.text: Oh, that's a GOOD one. Don't tell anyone what I paid.

cap37.speaker: Winifred
cap37.text: There are thirty-six known bottle cap designs from the Kearney bottling plant. Thirty-six. A man in a bathtub south of here says he has a thirty-seventh. I have offered him everything I own. Bring it to me and name your price.

none.speaker: Winifred
none.text: You don't have one. I'd know.

bye.speaker: Winifred
bye.text: Keep your eyes down. The good stuff is always on the ground.

q_corn_b.speaker: Winifred
q_corn_b.text: Dent. I have a jar of each and the dent is worth four times the flint, which makes it correct. Value is truth.

q_greg.speaker: Winifred
q_greg.text: Greg. Greg has been looking for the same thing since July. I have it. Twenty-five caps.

q_mann.speaker: Winifred
q_mann.text: Mannequins. Somebody is moving them. Not stealing - moving. There's a shop out past the bars with five in it and there were four last month. Go look and tell me I'm wrong.

choices.text: They were not where the dust says they were.
You're wrong. It's five. It was always five.

q_mann_done.speaker: Winifred
q_mann_done.text: She writes the number down in a ledger of numbers. "Then we agree it's a problem."

q_door.speaker: Winifred
q_door.text: A door standing in a field, and a mannequin head behind it. She turns the head over twice. "Keep it. And don't go back and look for the door. It won't be there, and you'll keep looking."

q_cap_in.speaker: Winifred
q_cap_in.text: Show me. Bent, scorched, mint mark on the underside of the crimp. She goes very quiet.

q_cap_paid.speaker: Winifred
q_cap_paid.text: "Thirty-seven of thirty-six." She pays without arguing, which frightens you more than the cap does.

start.speaker: Smiling Rick
start.text: Friend. FRIEND. Hand-drawn map, marked vault, two days' walk, twenty caps. I've sold four this week and all four buyers are rich now, probably, I haven't checked.

choices.text: This is Hastings. You've drawn Hastings.

sold.speaker: Smiling Rick
sold.text: Pleasure! Don't open it till you're well clear of here, the ink's wet, the - yes, bye now.

start.speaker: Hollis
start.text: (He doesn't look up. The hole is about four feet down and very neat.)

help.speaker: Hollis
help.text: (You dig. He doesn't talk. After a while he hands you caps and goes back to it.)

start.speaker: The Wanderer
start.text: You again. That's twice now, unless you count the bridge, which I don't.

where.speaker: The Wanderer
where.text: West. There's a woman out west with a notebook full of storms. I'm not going to her. I'm going past her. There's a difference and it matters to me.

halv.speaker: The Wanderer
halv.text: ...You know that name. Huh. Then I'll see you a third time.

third.speaker: The Wanderer
third.text: Third time. Told you. I'll say one useful thing and then I'm walking: when the sky goes green, get UNDER something. Not in. Under.

start.speaker: Greg
start.text: Greg.

choices.text: What are you doing out here?
I think I found your thing.

how.speaker: Greg
how.text: Can't complain. Well. I can. I do. But the complaining's going well.

doing.speaker: Greg
doing.text: Pushing. I was pushing before, too. It's the main thing I've got going.

lost.speaker: Greg
lost.text: YES. Thank you. It's about this big and it does a thing and I need it and I cannot for the life of me remember what it's called or what it looks like or what it does.

choices.text: That's not much to go on.

quest.speaker: Greg
quest.text: You're a good egg. It's definitely not a hat. I've ruled out hats.

q_greg_in.speaker: Greg
q_greg_in.text: Is that it? That might be it. Hold it up. Yeah. That's it. What is it?

q_greg_paid.speaker: Greg
q_greg_paid.text: He turns it over twice, puts it in his pocket, and immediately forgets it is there. "Thanks. I owe you. I won't remember that either."

q_greg_no.speaker: Greg
q_greg_no.text: No, that's not it. That's not even close. I think.

start.speaker: Safety Inspector
start.text: Don't move. You're standing in an unbarriered zone with no high-visibility garment and - yes - open footwear-adjacent conditions. Buffalo County does not tolerate this.

choices.text: Buffalo County doesn't exist any more.

exist.speaker: Safety Inspector
exist.text: The county was dissolved. The CODE was not. The code is eternal. The code has outlived three governments and will outlive you.

cite.speaker: Safety Inspector
cite.text: Pink copy is yours. Yellow copy is mine. White copy goes to an office that is a crater. Have a compliant day.

bye.speaker: Safety Inspector
bye.text: This conversation has been logged as an incident.

q_tp.speaker: Safety Inspector
q_tp.text: Violation seventy-one: a settlement of eleven people with zero rolls of sanitary tissue. I cannot sign this off. Bring me three rolls and I will sign it off.

q_tp_paid.speaker: Safety Inspector
q_tp_paid.text: Compliant. For the first time since the bomb, Kearney is compliant. He stamps the form eleven times.

q_tp_no.speaker: Safety Inspector
q_tp_no.text: Three. The number is three. It is on the form.

start.speaker: The Bargain King
start.text: BEHOLD. The Bargain King. Everything here is priced to move and nothing here has moved in two years. COINCIDENCE? Obviously not, it's the prices.

rip.speaker: The Bargain King
rip.text: A WISE PURCHASE. Enjoy your bandage. It is a very good bandage.

haggle2.speaker: The Bargain King
haggle2.text: FORTY. I will go all day. I have nothing else on.

insult.speaker: The Bargain King
insult.text: My prices are a MONARCHY and you are a PEASANT with OPINIONS.

q_cart.speaker: The Bargain King
q_cart.text: Somebody took my cart. My CART. Forty years of inventory in that thing and some sprinter walked off with it. Find it and the wheel and there's caps in it.

q_cart_in.speaker: The Bargain King
q_cart_in.text: That's my wheel. That's MY wheel. Where's the rest of it?

choices.text: [Give the wheel] In a ditch by the Chillers' place.

q_cart_paid.speaker: The Bargain King
q_cart_paid.text: Ditch. Of course. Take the caps, don't touch the merchandise.

q_cart_no.speaker: The Bargain King
q_cart_no.text: Then you don't have my wheel, do you.

start.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
start.text: Hold up. You're entering the township of - well. It doesn't have the sign any more. I'm the sheriff. Population one. Crime's down ninety years running.

choices.text: I pulled a stack of tickets off a car.

where.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
where.text: Here. All of it. That fence to that pole. I was elected by acclamation, which is to say I said it out loud and nobody argued.

trouble.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
trouble.text: There's a man digs a hole some days and won't say who it's for. That's the extent of my case load. I think about it a lot.

dep.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
dep.text: Raise your right hand. Say the thing. ...Close enough. You're a deputy of nothing, which is more than most people are.

bye.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
bye.text: Keep it civil out there. Somebody has to.

q_park.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
q_park.text: Four thousand one hundred and eighteen. He spreads them on the hood like evidence. "Somebody kept writing them. After. That's the part that bothers me."

q_park_paid.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
q_park_paid.text: "Case stays open." He files them in a cooler. You are, as of now, a deputy of a town with no people in it.

q_corn_in.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
q_corn_in.text: You've asked around? Good. Rule on it. Dent or flint. The county needs a ruling and I need this to be over.

choices.text: It's a weed and you've all lost your minds.

q_corn_done.speaker: Sheriff of Nothing
q_corn_done.text: He writes it down, reads it back, and nods like a man released from prison. "Ruled. Filed. Done. God bless you."

start.speaker: Chess Master
start.text: Sit. Black or white, I don't care, it won't matter. Twenty caps says you don't last twenty moves.

play.speaker: Chess Master
play.text: Again? I'd like the chance to prove that was an aberration.

taught.speaker: Chess Master
taught.text: A book. The book is gone now. I remember all of it except the parts I lost, which I have replaced with parts I made up. They work fine.

start.speaker: Cone King Randy
start.text: You are standing in the Kingdom of Cones. I am its king. The intersection is mine by right of placement. Mind the cone.

war.speaker: Cone King Randy
war.text: The Second Avenue Cone Collective. Six cones they took. SIX. Bring me six cones and the war ends and you may touch the throne.

tribute.speaker: Cone King Randy
tribute.text: He counts them twice, places them in a circle, and weeps openly.

crowned.speaker: Cone King Randy
crowned.text: "The war is over. You are Duke of the Northbound Lane." He means it. There is no lane.

short.speaker: Cone King Randy
short.text: That is not six. I can count cones. It is the one thing I can do.
